original: - L-Glutamine ([watch Dr. Rhonda vid](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=5DVUEKrekYw&ra=m)): The absolute premier energy substrate for enterocytes and activated immune cells. It bypasses complex digestive steps, converting directly into alpha-ketoglutarate (α-KG) inside the mitochondria to power the citric acid cycle. This immediate cellular energy hit actively drives the repair of the gut mucosal barrier and prevents LPS translocation.
rewrite: - L-Glutamine ([watch Dr. Rhonda vid](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=5DVUEKrekYw&ra=m)) is the main fuel for your enterocytes, and for your immune cells when they're activated. It doesn't have to go through the complicated digestive steps other nutrients do. Inside the mitochondria, it gets turned straight into alpha-ketoglutarate, or α-KG. The α-KG goes into the citric acid cycle, which is how the mitochondria make their energy. The cells get that energy right away, and they need it to repair the gut lining and keep LPS out.

original: - Butyrate & SCFAs: While the small intestine runs on glutamine, the large intestine relies on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate. Getting these via raw resistant starch fermentation or your home-brewed SIBO yogurt fuels colonocytes, locks down the lower gut barrier, and systematically suppresses inflammatory signals.
rewrite: - The colonocytes lining your large intestine rely on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate, while your small intestine runs on glutamine. Your gut bacteria make SCFAs when they ferment raw resistant starch, and you get them from your home-brewed SIBO yogurt too. Besides feeding the colonocytes, they lock down the barrier in your lower gut and keep turning down inflammatory signals.

original: - TCA Cycle Intermediates (Malic & Citric Acid): Organic acids like malate and citrate feed directly into the exact same mitochondrial energy pathways as glutamine. Consuming clean, sour profiles—such as organic malic acid, tart cherries, or green apples—provides rapid, alternative fuel to gut epithelial cells, accelerating mucosal healing from a different biochemical angle.
rewrite: - The point of eating clean sour stuff like organic malic acid, tart cherries or green apples is to give the cells lining your gut another fast fuel, one that speeds up healing of the lining by a different biochemical route than glutamine. That works because malic and citric acid are TCA cycle intermediates. The TCA cycle is another name for the citric acid cycle, so these organic acids go directly into the same energy pathway in the mitochondria that glutamine feeds.
